name: Bina (Papua New Guinea)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Dutton, T.E. 1971. Languages of south-east Papua: a preliminary report. In T.E. Dutton, C.L. Voorhoeve & S.A. Wurm, Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 14, 1-46. Pacific Linguistics A-28.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bina mentioned once, in the village list (p. 24): 'Also one Bina speaker claiming linguistic relationship with Magori.' No phonology of Magori or Bina. The stress statements found elsewhere in this volume (e.g. 'Bi-syllabic words generally have stress on the last syllable') are in Voorhoeve's West Irian notes and concern other languages. Whole-volume scan copied from the ouma1237 check folder (originally ANU hdl 1885/145019).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and JSON for bina1271 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Only reference: Dutton 1976, rated 'a wordlist or less'; status extinct (Moseley 2010). The Todaeva 1963 Paoan article attached to bina1271 in the our source list extract is a mis-tagged record (Mongolic, China) and irrelevant.
Stub citing Ethnologue 25 only; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Dutton, T. 1982. Borrowing in Austronesian and non-Austronesian languages of coastal south-east mainland Papua New Guinea. In A. Halim, L. Carrington & S.A. Wurm (eds), Papers from the Third International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics, vol. 1, 109-177. Pacific Linguistics C-74.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bina (BIN) is a comparandum in loanword tables only; the synchronic-phonology appendix (pp. 162-163) covers the Mailuan NAN languages and says nothing about stress. Its bibliography identifies the primary Bina data: 'Thomson, N.P. 1971. Unpublished vocabularies - Bina, Medua (=Morawa), Ma, Neme'a, Domu.'

sources.citation: Dutton, T.E. 1976. Austronesian languages: eastern part of south-eastern mainland Papua. In Wurm (ed.), NGAL Vol. 2, 321-333. Pacific Linguistics C-39. DOI 10.15144/PL-C39.321
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey chapter: Bina 'much further east.. inland of the western end of Orangerie Bay', only two surviving speakers (Tabi Koakoa at Nabai and his sister at Gogosiba); lexicostatistical percentages. Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Dutton, T.E. 1976. Magori and similar languages of south-east Papua. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, Vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 581-636. Pacific Linguistics C-39. DOI 10.15144/PL-C39.581
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 4.5.2.6.1 'Phonological evidence' (p. 594) treats Ouma, Magori, Yoba and Bina jointly: five vowels, shared consonant set, glottal stop suspect, all syllables open, no clusters. No mention of stress, accent, tone or pitch anywhere in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent scanned text with spacing-tolerant regex: zero hits). Bina data are a comparative wordlist (pp. 618-626), pronoun tables and a handful of clause examples without any accent marking. Glottolog rates this source 'a wordlist or less' for Bina.

sources.citation: Thomson, N.P. 1971. Unpublished vocabularies - Bina, Medua (=Morawa), Ma, Neme'a, Domu. (field notes; cited in Dutton 1982 bibliography)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The primary Bina data underlying Dutton 1976; the only place a field transcription with stress marks or a phonetic note could exist, since the language is extinct and no further data can be collected.

sources.note: Dutton's pre-1971 wordlist collection for the area; may carry phonetic transcriptions with stress marks for Magori, though Bina was only located after 1971 so Bina coverage is doubtful.

sources.citation: Capell, A. 1969. A survey of New Guinea languages. Sydney: Sydney University Press (pp. 26-35, sketches of AN and NAN phonologies of south-east Papua, per Dutton 1976 fn. 22)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only phonological survey Dutton points to for the area; could give a regional stress generalisation for Central Papuan AN languages, but it predates the discovery of Bina and would not be Bina-specific.

sources.citation: Dutton, T.E. & N.P. Thomson, field materials on Bina, Yoba and Ouma (c. 1970-1975), Australian National University / PARADISEC (Dutton collection, cf. hdl 1885/123373)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Dutton 1976 (p. 581) says he and Thomson collected 'similar materials from the few surviving members' of Bina, Yoba and Ouma, not yet analysed in detail; any recordings would allow an instrumental check of word accent. The ANU/PARADISEC collection metadata lists Magori and Ouma recordings but no Bina, so the existence of Bina audio is unconfirmed.
